chapters.name: Signs, Signals, and Pavement Markings
chapters.summary: What traffic lights, flashing signals, sign shapes and colors, and lane lines tell you to do.
keyPoints: A flashing red light means stop, then go when it is safe. A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful.
If a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop.
Double solid yellow lines mean no passing. A broken yellow line means you may pass when it is safe.

chapters.name: Right of Way and Turns
chapters.summary: Who goes first at intersections, four-way stops, roundabouts, crosswalks, and when turning.
keyPoints: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to stop goes first. If two arrive together, yield to the driver on your right.
In a roundabout, travel counterclockwise and yield to traffic already in the circle.
Always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk, marked or unmarked.

chapters.name: Speed, Lanes, and Parking
chapters.summary: The Basic Speed Law, special speed limits, lane use, passing, and parking rules including curb colors.
keyPoints: Basic Speed Law: never drive faster than is safe for current conditions, whatever the posted limit.
15 mph in alleys and at blind intersections and blind railroad crossings; 25 mph in most school zones when children are present.
Red curb: no stopping. White: passenger loading. Green: limited-time parking. Blue: disabled parking only.

chapters.name: Safe Driving and Sharing the Road
chapters.summary: Following distance, scanning, night and bad-weather driving, skids, and sharing the road with bicycles, motorcycles, trucks, and emergency vehicles.
keyPoints: Keep at least a three-second following distance, and more in bad weather.
Give bicyclists at least 3 feet when passing.
When an emergency vehicle with siren and lights approaches, pull to the right edge and stop.

chapters.name: Alcohol, Phones, and Licensing Laws
chapters.summary: Blood alcohol limits, implied consent, cell phone rules, seat belts and child seats, collision reporting, and insurance.
keyPoints: It is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08% or higher (21 and over) or 0.01% or higher if you are under 21.
Drivers may not hold a phone while driving; drivers under 18 may not use a phone at all, even hands-free.
Report a collision to the DMV within 10 days if anyone was hurt or killed or property damage is over $1,000.
